props.title: A Better Tomorrow
props.initialSlug: Two brothers collide as honor meets crime and revenge

sections.content: A Better Tomorrow (1986) revolutionized Hong Kong action cinema and launched John Woo's signature "heroic bloodshed" style. Chow Yun-fat's iconic portrayal of Mark Gor - with his matchstick-chewing swagger and dual-wielding gunplay - created the template for cool that influenced everything from The Matrix (1999) to John Wick (2014). The film's blend of brotherhood, betrayal, and balletic violence transformed action choreography globally, while its themes of loyalty and redemption between Ti Lung's reformed gangster and Leslie Cheung's righteous cop brother set the emotional foundation for countless crime dramas.

sections.content: The impact of A Better Tomorrow rippled through 1980s and 90s Hong Kong cinema, inspiring a wave of stylized crime films. Ringo Lam's City on Fire (1987) took the genre into grittier territory, while Young and Dangerous (1996) translated the themes for a new generation. The film's DNA is evident in contemporary Asian cinema like Internal Affairs (2002) and Drug War (2012), which maintain its focus on loyalty, duty, and the thin line between cop and criminal.

The film's technical innovations were equally revolutionary. Woo's approach to action - combining slow-motion, dynamic camera movement, and carefully choreographed violence - created a new visual language. This influence extends from Hong Kong contemporaries like Full Contact (1992) to Hollywood productions like Face/Off (1997) and Mission: Impossible 2 (2000), both directed by Woo himself after his transition to Hollywood. sections.content: Beyond action choreography, A Better Tomorrow established enduring archetypes in crime cinema. The brotherhood theme resonated across cultures, influencing films like Internal Affairs (2002), which Martin Scorsese remade as The Departed (2006). The film's stylish gunplay and emotional depth created a template for character-driven action, seen in everything from Leon: The Professional (1994) to The Man from Nowhere (2010).
